summary.name: VLC media player
summary.one_liner: VLC is a free, open-source, cross-platform multimedia player and framework from the non-profit VideoLAN project that plays most audio and video files and streaming protocols.
keywords: free alternative to paid media players
use_cases: play most audio and video files
summary.what_it_does: The page is the official VideoLAN site for VLC, describing it as a free, open-source, cross-platform multimedia player and framework that plays most multimedia files and various streaming protocols. The current listed version is 3.0.24 for Windows (43 MB), with a 2026-09-22 release note describing over 130 security fixes, an FFmpeg upgrade from 4.4 to 8.1.2, and new features such as ATRAC decoding and SRT listener mode. The page also lists related VideoLAN libraries and codecs: libbluray 1.5.0, libaacs 0.12.0, libdvdcss 1.6.0, libdvdread 7.1, and the dav1d AV1 decoder, plus the new dav2d AV2 decoder in early development. VideoLAN is funded by donations and asks users to donate, contribute, or spread the word.
notable: Free and open source, funded by donations from a non-profit organization
Bundles and maintains related libraries such as dav1d (AV1 decoder) and dav2d (AV2 decoder)
Plays DVD and Blu-ray related media through libdvdcss and libbluray
Cross-platform framework that plays most media formats and streaming protocols
caveats: The page names Windows explicitly; macOS and Linux are not named in the page text itself (macOS is mentioned only in a release note about a MIDI fix)
Early-stage work: dav2d is described as still early work
